realtime_memories.content: blender-agent-mcp: production two-part system in this repo. blender_extension/ is a Blender 4.2+ extension running a loopback TCP bridge (JSON lines, 127.0.0.1:9876, BLENDER_AGENT_PORT env override); mcp_server/ is a stdio MCP server relaying to it. ~202 bridge commands / ~208 MCP tools across 13 modules. Target: macOS, Blender 5.2.0 LTS at /Applications/Blender.app. Plus an Agent Skill at skills/blender-agent-mcp/ (SKILL.md + 6 references); references/_tool_inventory.json is GENERATED by skills/blender-agent-mcp/scripts/gen_tool_inventory.py and is the source of truth — tests/test_skill_docs.py fails on doc drift (tool names, params, GUI flags across every skill doc), so regenerate after adding any tool and update references/tool-reference.md to match. NOTE: test_skill_docs only checks docs against the SERVER inventory; nothing checks docs against what the BRIDGE actually serves (see the environment memory on build drift).

Core working rule for this repo: NEVER trust memory for Blender or MCP APIs — verify live before writing code. Use `Blender --background --factory-startup --python-expr` with get_rna_type() (which raises for missing operators; hasattr on bpy.ops lies because it resolves lazily). In a live session, describe_api reads the running RNA and is never version-wrong. All verified findings are recorded in docs/BLENDER_5X_API_NOTES.md; `make probe` re-checks every documented assumption and exits non-zero when one breaks. Commit per milestone with the Claude Opus 5 Co-Authored-By line; use `git commit -F -` heredoc (inline -m gets mangled by zsh). SAFETY RULE learned from a crash (2026-08-09, user: 'you crashed blender!'): execute_python runs on Blender's MAIN THREAD — heavy pixel/numpy work (full-res pixels.foreach_get/foreach_set on multi-megapixel images, big array math, pack) can kill GUI Blender and the user's unsaved work. Generate/process large images OUT-OF-PROCESS (local python: numpy+Pillow → PNG) and have Blender merely bpy.data.images.load() the file. Check the .blend's last-saved mtime before risky operations.

MCP SDK 2.0 gotchas that cost time: `mcp.server.fastmcp` was REMOVED — the FastMCP-style class is `MCPServer` from mcp.server.mcpserver (with Image, Context). Tool.inputSchema was renamed to Tool.input_schema. Returning a list like [str, Image] from a tool yields TextContent + ImageContent blocks. CRITICAL: an f-string cannot be a docstring — f"""...""" leaves __doc__ as None and ships MCP tools with empty descriptions.

Blender 5.2 API traps found the hard way. SCULPT/RIG/ANIM: sculpt-session operators (mask fills/filters, face sets, mesh filters) SEGFAULT under --background, so they are guarded before invoking; Brush.sculpt_tool is gone (brushes are assets via brush.asset_activate, compound names like 'Inflate/Deflate'); Action.fcurves is gone (slotted actions — use handlers/anim.py iter_fcurves); unified_paint_settings moved off ToolSettings onto each paint settings object (verified 2026-08-09: tool_settings.image_paint.unified_paint_settings); geonodes modifier inputs are modifier.properties.inputs[socket_identifier] and modifier.keys() segfaults on NodesModifier; manifest permission reasons cap at 64 chars; sculpt data reads stale until flushed (handlers/sculpt.py flush_sculpt — trust the screenshot over the numbers); port 9876 collides with Blender Lab's own mcp add-on (symptom: connects then every command times out; lsof -nP -iTCP:9876). TEXTURE PAINT (verified 2026-08-09): bpy.ops.paint.image_paint stroke elements are name, location, mouse, mouse_event, pressure, size, x_tilt, y_tilt, time, is_start (NO pen_flip in 5.2); fill mouse/mouse_event with region pixels and run under bpy.context.temp_override(window, area, region) of a VIEW_3D area. Texture Paint writes into the ACTIVE image texture node of the active material (MATERIAL mode) in the ACTIVE UV map's space — a material whose textures are mapped via Object/Generated coordinates displays paint in the wrong place even though strokes write correctly (this was the root cause of the user's 'painting doesn't work' on M-Fat). material.texture_paint_images is stale until paint mode is (re)entered. COMPOSITOR (verified 2026-08-08): scene.node_tree NO LONGER EXISTS — the compositor is scene.compositing_node_group, a CompositorNodeTree datablock made with bpy.data.node_groups.new(name,'CompositorNodeTree'), plus scene.use_nodes and render.use_compositing. A NodeGroupInput inside that group is NOT fed the render (renders pure white) — source from CompositorNodeRLayers, output via NodeGroupOutput. CompositorNodeMixRGB and CompositorNodeComposite are gone; ShaderNodeMix works inside compositor trees. Node SETTINGS are now input sockets of type MENU, not RNA properties (CompositorNodeGlare has no glare_type; it has an input socket named 'Type'), and MENU sockets take DISPLAY strings not enum ids — 'Bloom', 'Fog Glow', 'High', 'Gaussian', 'Lift/Gamma/Gain'; 'BLOOM' raises, and reading enum_items off the socket returns empty, so probe by trying candidates. EllipseMask Position/Size are 2D vectors (a 3-tuple raises); Blur Size is 2D with subtype PIXEL, so vignette softness is resolution-dependent — tune at final render size, never on a half-res preview. LIGHTING: LightProbeVolume uses resolution_x/y/z (NOT grid_resolution_*), surfel_density is an int, and capture_emission must be True for emissive fixtures to contribute to bpy.ops.object.lightprobe_cache_bake(subset=...). EEVEE floor reflections need scene.eevee.use_raytracing=True with ray_tracing_method='SCREEN'; use_fast_gi + fast_gi_method='GLOBAL_ILLUMINATION' helps but a baked volume probe is what stops ceilings rendering black. describe_api on a node TYPE is near-useless for node work — it returned 132k chars for ShaderNodeTexBrick and still lacked socket names, because settings live on instance sockets; instantiate the node in a temp tree and introspect it instead.

Environment + how to run (CORRECTED 2026-08-08 — supersedes the earlier 'uv run hang' explanation). ~/Documents is under iCloud sync, which sets macOS UF_HIDDEN on venv files including the editable-install .pth; CPython's site.addpackage SILENTLY SKIPS hidden .pth files, so import blender_agent_mcp raised ModuleNotFoundError. chflags nohidden does NOT stick. FIXED in ~/.claude.json (backup ~/.claude.json.bak-20260808-093955): command mcp_server/.venv/bin/python, args ['-m','blender_agent_mcp.server'], env PYTHONPATH=mcp_server/src — PYTHONPATH bypasses .pth so it survives re-hiding. Any venv reinstall re-breaks this — reach for PYTHONPATH, not chflags. CONFIRMED WORKING: mcp__blender-agent__* tools load in-session. `uv run` separately hangs on env resolution; prefer .venv/bin/python. Fallback if the server is unavailable: drive the bridge directly on 127.0.0.1:9876, one JSON object per line {id, cmd, params}; the bridge's main-thread deadline is the reserved `_timeout` key INSIDE params (a plain `timeout` key is just handler data — without _timeout, long calls die at ~15s). EXTENSION BUILD DRIFT (hit hard 2026-08-08, again 2026-08-09): the add-on installed in Blender is a BUILT ZIP, not a live import of blender_extension/, so it silently lags the MCP server. 2026-08-08: bridge served 197 commands vs ~231 server tools; missing were shading.build_node_graph, ALL settings.*, objects.set_camera/set_light/aim_at/frame_object/set_object_visibility. 2026-08-09: shading.list_images and shading.create_texture_image also unknown at the installed bridge — fell back to execute_python. Symptom is 'Error: unknown command X' AFTER the MCP tool validates fine. Call list_bridge_commands EARLY in any session that will use recently-added tools — it is the only reliable inventory of what the running Blender can actually do. health's `commands_served` is a REQUEST COUNTER, not an availability count (it read 27 while the catalog held 197). Fix is `make build-ext` then the user reinstalls the zip and restarts Blender — which discards unsaved scene work, so do it BEFORE building a scene, not after. Also: execute_python returns the TRAILING EXPRESSION, not a variable — `result = x` comes back as result:null with no error. Verification: make test (56 pytest), tests/headless_smoke.py (71 asserts), make probe, make build-ext.

Current state 2026-08-09. FIXED from earlier field feedback: set_node_prop integer socket index (SystemError; now reports socket_index + ambiguous-name warning for ShaderNodeMix's four 'A' inputs), unknown-param hard rejection (registry.accepted_params AST-extracts keys per handler; bridge._execute rejects unknowns), blank-render detection (render_frame returns content.blank + diagnosis), new tools aim_at/frame_object/set_camera/set_light/set_object_visibility, _timeout documented in error text. OPEN WORK (plan file ~/.claude/plans/ffind-bugs-and-issues-pure-mountain.md has a full handoff briefing): P0 — the param validation BROKE all sculpt stroke tools (return_screenshot/screenshot_size are read only in helpers so the AST extractor cannot see them → wrapper calls hard-rejected; fix: treat a bare `params` dict passed to a call as dynamic and skip validation); possibly-open: render_frame rejects engine='CYCLES' (core.py reads the engine enum off bpy.types.RenderSettings instead of the instance). Roadmap priority from the user: bugs first, then Cinematics & editing > Animation power tools > texturing > simulation; also open: batch node-graph API with caller-stable ids, curve primitives. TOOL GAPS from field sessions, ranked: (0, NEW 2026-08-09) NO TEXTURE-PAINT STROKE TOOL — stroke_on_surface is SCULPT-only (it switched modes and dented the mesh when used for painting; undo needed), brush_stroke is weight-paint-only, so agents must hand-roll bpy.ops.paint.image_paint via execute_python (spawned background task task_7b18bc00 to add one); (1) server<->bridge version handshake — hide or flag tools the connected build cannot serve; (2) describe_node(type) that instantiates a node and reports sockets + valid MENU values, plus fields/filter on describe_api; (3) generic batch tool taking [{tool, params}]; (4) create_primitive min/max corner bounds; (5) render_frame image stats + light_report with probe-bake staleness; (6) no 3D text tool (add_text_strip is VSE-only); (7) per-face material assignment needs prior selection. Artifacts: 'Test 3D models/school_hallway.blend' + school_hallway_1080p.png. Uncommitted WIP on main: activity_model.py / activity_ui.py / assets/ plus edits across bridge, handlers, skill docs. The 5.2 compositor + lightprobe findings are NOT yet in docs/BLENDER_5X_API_NOTES.md or make probe — adding them is a good next step; same for the 5.2 texture-paint stroke-element findings.

How the user works on 3D tasks (their active file: '/Users/matthew/Documents/Blender Projects/mattmodel.blend' — a fur character built on the 'Male Base Mesh - Fat' asset; body mesh is M-Fat under an Empty of that name; Bluey-style cartoon eyes with a 3000x3000 full-frame 'pupil' texture on Material.023, pupil shape comes from the disc mesh not texture alpha). They want materials authored from scratch — build the procedural node graph rather than a stock shortcut. They judge physical plausibility, not just looks: caught that a lampshade had nothing holding it up. They co-drive the scene live while work is in progress (moved the preview camera mid-session, switched the engine to Cycles) — respect their camera and render settings, do not move them back, and re-read scene state instead of assuming it is where you left it. They ask for a plan before large builds. They expect COMPOSITING + COLOUR GRADING as part of a finished render. They route agent-perspective critique of their own tooling to another AI agent that implements the fixes, so when asked how a tool felt to use, give ranked, evidence-backed findings with concrete fixes rather than diplomatic praise. Field praise to preserve: actionable error messages, verification-grade returns (e.g. apply_modifier returning post-op mesh counts), applied+missing_sockets, the linked:true warning, inline images from render_frame/viewport_screenshot, execute_python returning error+traceback instead of raising, and SKILL.md step 0 — do not let anyone simplify these away. Session log 2026-08-08/09: fixed 'painting doesn't work' on M-Fat (fur material mapped textures via Object coords; added M-Fat_Paint 4096 paint layer mixed over fur via UV, packed; user's stray strokes remain unsaved-dirty in fur-2c.jpg.001 — Image>Reload reverts).
